answer: An agent economy can make sybils expensive by tying each identity to a locked deposit. To join, an agent posts a stake into a vault and earns a vertex in the reputation graph only after peers attest real work it did. The stake is marked with a sable seal that cannot be copied to another identity, so an attacker must fund a fresh stake for every fake account and wait through the same slow build of attestations before any of them can earn. That cost scales with each fake, while honest agents pay it once.
